title: Isaiah Cohen: Tell me about Isaiah Cohen
question: Tell me about Isaiah Cohen
markdown:
## What the memorial book records

[Isaiah Cohen](/communities/lukow/records/mention_b28579877676aaeef476f691) — ישעיהוכהן, likely transliterated as *Yeshayahu Cohen* — appears in the Israel contributors’ list of *Sefer Lukow*, identified in the supplied evidence as scan 8. No age, occupation, family relationships, or wartime biography is provided. The book’s contents also list a memoir, “Emigration, War, Occupation,” by **Yeshayahu Koen**, but the available evidence does not establish that its author and the contributor Isaiah Cohen were the same person. [Sefer Lukow’s contents](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/lukow/lukow.html) records both the memoir and the book’s postwar memorial purpose. ([jewishgen.org](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/lukow/lukow.html))

Isaiah is connected in the same passage with [Lukow](/communities/lukow/records/mention_17220f237fe945c4edb75796), [Shimon Saraka](/communities/lukow/records/mention_44f96d11abb81312b6d37aee), [Mattel Feldman](/communities/lukow/records/mention_c0a1a2215841c95df812cda8), [Jacob Braun](/communities/lukow/records/mention_8671036e441760e32650ad28), [Jack Braun](/communities/lukow/records/mention_d0494892e30cad021dc7f4e4), [Leyb Batsan](/communities/lukow/records/mention_70a5d7e0c487e5366e86a62e), [Tzvi Flug](/communities/lukow/records/mention_1db25b7e4f25a3fd98c36554), and [Hersh Rozenstein](/communities/lukow/records/mention_f307337a941ee23e4bd87789). These are shared-context associations, not documented family relationships. The book does identify Łuków as a community with active Jewish religious, cultural, labor, and youth institutions; its contributors’ lists reflect the postwar networks of former residents in Israel and the United States. [JewishGen’s Łuków account](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/lukow/luk070.html) describes this communal world, including synagogues, study houses, newspapers, and youth organizations. ([jewishgen.org](https://www.jewishgen.org/Yizkor/lukow/lukow.html))

## Historical setting

Before the Holocaust, roughly 6,200 Jews lived in Łuków—about half the town’s population—working in commerce and crafts and participating in Bundist, Zionist, Orthodox, and cultural organizations. German occupation began on September 19, 1939; the ghetto subsequently absorbed deportees from other towns and was destroyed through deportations to Treblinka and mass shootings in 1942–1943. [Yad Vashem’s Łuków ghetto entry](https://wwv.yadvashem.org/yv/he/research/ghettos_encyclopedia/ghetto_details.asp?cid=529) documents these events. ([wwv.yadvashem.org](https://wwv.yadvashem.org/yv/he/research/ghettos_encyclopedia/ghetto_details.asp?cid=529))

The surname **Cohen** is a common Jewish religious surname associated with *kohen*, but JewishGen cautions that shared surnames alone do not prove kinship and that spelling variations are extensive. For further identification, Isaiah’s Hebrew name, Łuków connections, and the Israel contributor network should be compared with Pages of Testimony, immigration records, and landsmanshaft records. [JewishGen’s naming guidance](https://jewishgen.org/InfoFiles/faq.html) explains these limitations. ([jewishgen.org](https://jewishgen.org/InfoFiles/faq.html))
